Source. Because the non-strict parser sees a literal space, `uri_cleanup()` rewrites that byte to `%20`. This creates the first `%` later consumed as a scope-ID delimiter and changes the URI bytes to `59 3a 2f 2f 5b 3a 25 32 30 f8 5d`.
The parser switches from the original witness to the cleaned copy, so all later authority parsing sees bracketed host bytes `[:%20<0xF8>]` rather than the original `[: <0xF8>]`.

hostend = colon ? colon : path_start;
if (!parse_host (p, hostend - p, flags, host, error))
anchors.note: Authority parsing is on a bracketed host (`*p == '['`), so `parse_host()` receives the 7-byte cleaned literal `[:%20<0xF8>]`. Removing the brackets will therefore yield the 5-byte inner host `:%20<0xF8>`.
ASan allocation context. `g_strndup()` copies the inner 5 bytes `:%20<0xF8>` into heap buffer `addr`, allocating 6 addressable bytes including the trailing NUL.

Root cause begins. The cleanup-added `%` at offset 1 is treated as a scope-ID separator, so `pct` points inside `:%20<0xF8>` and the in-place NUL write truncates `addr` to the prefix `":"` before validation.

The only IPv6 guard now examines `":"`. `g_hostname_is_ip_address(":")` returns true because `ghostutils.c:705-763` enters the IPv6 colon path, sets `skipped = TRUE` for the bare-colon case, and succeeds at EOF; `strchr (addr, ':')` is also non-null, so rejection is skipped.

After that truncated prefix has been accepted, the code restores `%` into the same buffer, finds no second `%` in `20<f8>`, and skips the only decode path because the suffix starts with `%20` rather than `%25`. The malformed host therefore stays `:%20<0xF8>`.
Instead of rejecting or rebuilding from a validated zone identifier, `parse_host()` aliases the same 6-byte allocation as the parsed host.
The success path returns that same pointer through the caller-supplied `host` out-parameter; in `g_uri_parse_relative()` this parameter is `&uri->host` at `guri.c:1163-1166`.

During `g_uri_to_string()`, the surviving host still contains `:`, so GLib takes the IP-literal branch, adds surrounding brackets, and sends the same host buffer to URI escaping with only `:` allowed verbatim.

The escaping wrapper passes `_uri_encoder()` the same host pointer, `allow_utf8 = TRUE`, and a source-level length computed by `strlen (host)`. For the reconstructed host `:%20<0xF8>`, `strlen()` yields 5, so the encoder loop ends just after the trailing `0xF8` byte.

After earlier loop iterations consume `:%20`, `p` reaches the final byte `0xF8` with `end - p == 1`. `g_utf8_get_char_validated ((gchar *)p, 1)` returns the partial-sequence sentinel `(gunichar)-2`; because `gunichar` is `guint32`, the `> 0` test still succeeds, `g_utf8_skip[0xF8]` contributes `5`, and `_uri_encoder()` requests a 5-byte append from that tail pointer.

Sink. Step 13's `g_string_append_len (..., len = 5)` call forwards the same tail pointer and length into `g_string_insert_len()`, so this `memcpy` attempts to read 5 bytes beginning at the trailing `0xF8` in the allocation from step 5. The saved ASan trace reports that 5-byte read and places the first invalid byte immediately past the 6-byte region.

The vulnerable scope-ID handling treats the first `%` as a temporary terminator and validates only the truncated prefix. The later block at lines 416-423 then restores the suffix with only secondary `%` and `%25` checks instead of parsing and decoding a ZoneID.
ASan crash site. During URI reserialization, `g_string_insert_len()` performs the witnessed 5-byte read from data derived from the `parse_host()` heap buffer.
At the final UTF-8 branch, _uri_encoder() asks to append len=g_utf8_skip[*p] bytes from the trailing host byte even though only end - p bytes remain in the source span.
